Hi,

As you probably know a lot of users moved to Voat because of SJW censorship and drama on Reddit. Just like Reddit, Voat is vulnerable to the same problems, and it's matter of time until Voat corrupts. A system is needed to prevent what happens on Reddit from repeating on Voat. Right now subverse owners & moderators are dictators, and users are at their mercy.

Giving users the power to take down abusive owner/moderators via democratic voting should help to keep them in check.

The implementation method could be something like Approval Voting System.

Common counter-argument refutes

"Make your own board"

Some may argue that being able to to create new alternative subverses is a solution. It is not a real solution because of user base, network effect, name recognition, and so on. It just won't take off. Basically it's voluntarily banning yourself.

"It's abusable!"

Need a majority vs need a single person. Also the single person is permanent, and elections are temporary. It's much less abusable then the current system. In fact if someone wanted to attack a subverse it's much easier to just spam it, requires waaaay less users.

"What incentive will board owners have?"

That argument implies the incentive is to be a a power tripping dictator. That's an incentive we want to get rid off, so that's a good thing. The incentive should be the same as any other user on the board - to have a place for discussing your interest.
Democratic Election of Subverses Owners & Moderators

Moderators are "owners" and the creators of subverses own them because they created them. Having a free speech oriented site does not require a bureaucracy to approve the control of a portion of it; think libertarian and not like a big government democrat.
"because they created them", well there's your problem. It doesn't mean they can do a good job.

It's called democracy, it takes a majority, and it's reversible. Majority is much smaller than a single or few people, so it's much less abusable.

Not going to happen, and nor should it. Some sub creators invest a hell of a lot of effort into creating, monitoring, nurturing and growing their subverses. What's the incentive when any random group can come along and take it off them? If the user base is dissatisfied with a given sub, they will move - that's how half of Reddit ended up on Voat.
